---
title: "Keeping rows"
---

{{< include ../_setup.qmd >}}

`keep` takes a condition and keeps the rows where it holds.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
sales |> keep(region == "West")
```

### Python

```{python}
sales >> keep(col.region == "West")
```

:::

Conditions combine with `and` and `or`, and either language's negation reverses
one.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
sales |> keep(revenue > 150 & cost < 100)
```

### Python

```{python}
sales >> keep((col.revenue > 150) & (col.cost < 100))
```

:::

There is no separate verb for dropping rows. Removing the rows where something
is true is keeping the rows where it is false, and one verb says both.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
sales |> keep(!(product == "Widget"))
```

### Python

```{python}
sales >> keep(~(col.product == "Widget"))
```

:::
